quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: ______ is a guarantee that another driver sees you.

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.explanation: No single action guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it might.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's space cushion should:

options.text: Always stay the same.
Change based on riding conditions.
Not be necessary in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.explanation: Increase your space cushion if your motorcycle needs longer to stop, the pavement is wet, you cannot see ahead clearly, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright and reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed for safety.

questions.question: The right footwear for riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Has long, loose laces.
Has short heels.
Has tall heels.
Is always sneakers.

questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels may catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show road rules like speed limits. They are white with black lettering. Follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT prevent a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Involve them in activities to slow their drinking and keep them busy while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: Good ways to stop drunk driving include arranging another ride, keeping them busy with activities, using any excuse to delay them, and getting friends to help. Waiting 15 minutes is not enough time to become safe to drive.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should NOT:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden moves.
Use both brakes.
Brake quickly.

questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Never brake quickly.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to riding during the day, you should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Allow more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.
Tailgate other vehicles.

questions.explanation: At night, ride more slowly and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Change your lane position as needed. Never tailgate.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: Passengers should ride in the sidecar. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following provides the best protection for a rider?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses are not as effective as a face shield.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag motion.
Ride on the shoulder instead of over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is not dangerous. If this happens, relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting your riding to less than six hours per day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks on long trips. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Avoid artificial stimulants because the effects can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it difficult to see.
Use only one lane position.
Reduce your speed.

questions.explanation: Ride slower at night and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when there is no oncoming traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding
When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals are not working

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down where drivers may not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: When entering a curve, how should a group of motorcyclists ride?

options.text: In a single-file formation
In a staggered formation
In pairs
On the shoulder

questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation during normal riding. Switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use the front brake only
Use the rear brake first
Release the throttle and use the front brake
Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together to stop quickly. Apply them firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock up.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the other driver will yield to you
It is not worth the effort
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you
It means the driver sees you

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow-moving cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly
Weave between the cars to pass quickly
Do not weave between the cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between the cars
questions.explanation: Weaving between cars is dangerous. You could hit an opening car door or get hit by a car pulling into traffic. You will not have room to react safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not just hold you up
Sit far back so you can keep your arms straight
Keep your knees away from the gas tank
Drag your feet on the ground

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not just hold you up
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: What happens to your steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire will make steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what should you do when following another vehicle?

options.text: Maintain a minimum four-second following distance.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Never worry about your following distance.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a minimum four-second following distance.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should stay at least four seconds behind other vehicles. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve which of the following?

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Worn tires.
Riding in the dark.
Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who have little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Maintain a longer following distance.
Increase their speed.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn passengers about upcoming hazards.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. The operator should keep a larger space cushion between their motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors to see what's around them?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars do.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road ahead and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars do.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Turn your head often to check these blind spots as part of your normal riding routine.
